commits.message:
chore: repo hardening — pinned actions, dependabot, community files

- Workflows: actions pinned by commit SHA (dependabot keeps them fresh);
  CI runs unfiltered since 'checks' is a required status check on main
- dependabot.yml: weekly github-actions + bun (root and website), grouped
- CODEOWNERS, SECURITY.md (private vulnerability reporting), CONTRIBUTING.md,
  CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md, PR/issue templates
feat(website): llms.txt + llms-full.txt for AI agent discoverability
chore(release): 1.0.0
chore: simplified code block on website

feat(website): "See the full docs" button in How it works

Links to the README on GitHub, the source of truth for the API and the
math. Solid CTA at the end of the explainer column, with the external
arrow to signal it leaves the site.
feat(website): vercel analytics

feat(core): fitIcon — re-grid packs drawn off the 24×24 canvas

Both endpoints of a morph must share a coordinate space. Packs on another
canvas (Heroicons solid 20, Carbon 32, Teenyicons 15) had no answer beyond
'keep both endpoints on that grid'. fitIcon maps a viewBox onto the shared
grid with the xMidYMid meet rule and returns a plain d, accepted anywhere
an icon is.

Skipping it never threw and never faked a rotation — Procrustes is
similarity-invariant, so a uniform grid change lands in sigma as an
unwanted zoom, with the target drawn outside the canvas.

Docs: drop Feather as a headline pack (archived; Lucide is its successor)
in favour of Tabler/Heroicons/Iconoir and the shadcn registry. Playground
attribution stays — the demo really does ship Feather icons.
chore(release): 1.1.0

feat(website): Heroicons replaces Feather in the studio

Feather is archived (Lucide is its successor) and was already dropped from
the headline copy; the studio now demos Heroicons outline instead — the
most popular of the newly documented compatible packs. Eight icons
extracted verbatim from heroicons@2.2.0 (MIT, Tailwind Labs), each
validated through the full pipeline (parse -> plan -> interpolate, no NaN)
before vendoring. Footer attribution follows what the demo actually ships.

fix(core): block transport — congruent icons stay rigid mid-flight

Under the global hybrid every subpath shared (θ, σ) but centroids still
lerped along the chord, so off-center parts drifted toward the center in
transit (an arrow's head sagged ~1px toward its shaft at t = 0.5).
Centroids now ride the shared similarity around the global centroid;
pinned by a new invariant: cross-subpath distances hold at t = 0.25/0.5/0.75.

v1.1.1

chore(website): consume morphicons from npm, auto-bump on publish

Replaces the vendored 0.1.0 tgz with the published package (exact pin,
1.1.1). publish.yml now points the website at each new release after
publishing; weekly dependabot on /website stays as backstop.
Feat/vue

fix(release): self-hosted star chart + unblock the website auto-bump (#9)

## Why

The **v1.2.0** release published to npm correctly, but the Publish job
ended red: its last step bumped the website's version pin and pushed it
straight to `main`, which the `protect-main` ruleset rejects without a
PR + the `checks` status check (`GH013`). The website stayed pinned to
`morphicons@1.1.1` while npm already served `1.2.0`.

Separately, the star-history chart in the README rendered broken:
`api.star-history.com` answers **HTTP 503 — "All GitHub API tokens are
rate-limited"** (it fails for any repo, not just this one), and GitHub's
image proxy caches that failure.

## What

**website pin → 1.2.0** — what the failed step would have done. `bun run
build` passes against it.

**publish.yml no longer bumps the pin.** Granting the GitHub Actions app
a bypass on the ruleset is not possible here: rulesets only accept an
`Integration` belonging to the owner *organization*, and this is a
personal repo — the API answers `422 "Actor GitHub Actions integration
must be part of the ruleset source or owner organization"`. Rather than
keep a step that can only ever fail, or introduce a long-lived PAT into
a repo that publishes via OIDC with no secrets at all, the step is
removed and **dependabot owns the bump**: `/website` moves from weekly
to daily, and dependabot's PRs do trigger CI, unlike anything pushed
with `GITHUB_TOKEN`. The site trails npm by at most a day. The reasoning
is recorded as a note at the end of the workflow so this isn't
rediscovered later.

**Star chart is now self-hosted** — `scripts/star-history.mjs` (`bun run
stars`) generates light/dark SVGs from this repo's own stargazer data,
zero dependencies, using the website's design tokens. It is
**deliberately static**: an entrance animation renders as a blank chart
in anything that snapshots at `t=0` (QuickLook, npm's README preview,
social cards). Verified with headless Chrome in both themes.
Regenerating it is a manual `bun run stars` — a cron workflow would hit
the very same push-to-main wall.

## Verification

`bun test` → 92 pass / 13,509 asserts · `bun run typecheck` (×4) ·
`biome check` clean · `website` builds against the new pin.

feat(website): SEO metadata, JSON-LD graph and Vue across the site

The title now opens with what people search for instead of the brand, and
the description fits under the ~155 char snippet limit.

Vue was invisible outside /roadmap since 1.2.0 shipped: it is now in the
description, the keywords and llms.txt, which gains its own quickstart with
the binding's real API (plain render function, Nuxt SSR).

JSON-LD grows from a lone SoftwareSourceCode into a three-node @graph:
SoftwareApplication carries the category and states MIT as a zero-price
Offer (the only place crawlers read "free" from), SoftwareSourceCode keeps
the repo, WebSite anchors the site. `<` is escaped per the Next 16 JSON-LD
guide.

The sitemap drops new Date(): every build claimed both pages had changed.
Dates are now hand-kept per route.

feat(website): keyword-carrying hero copy

The H1 held no term anyone searches for. It now leads with "Morph any SVG
icon", and the subhead names Lucide, Tabler and Heroicons before the math.
The OG image and its alt follow the same copy so the two never drift.

text-balance on the headline: the longer line otherwise dropped "other."
alone onto a second row.

chore: drop the star history chart from the README

Removes the self-hosted chart and everything that fed it: the README
section, the `bun run stars` script, scripts/star-history.mjs and the
two generated SVGs in assets/.

feat: Svelte 5 binding, bindings lifecycle hardening and landing tabs (v1.3.0)

- morphicons/svelte: MorphIcon with the three modes, exact SSR, a11y,
  lucide-svelte drop-in. Ships as .svelte source via the svelte export
  condition; optional peer svelte >= 5. All logic lives in typechecked
  shared.ts behind a thin rune shell.
- Lifecycle contract shared by React/Vue/Svelte (README): lazy driver on
  iconless mounts, controlled-wins precedence, pair invalidation on every
  exit from controlled mode — fixes dead iconless components, stale
  controlled state across mode switches and competing prop modes.
- Client coverage: mirrored mount suites on happy-dom for the three
  bindings + svelte controller suite with fakes + compile-time props
  pins; the svelte test loader compiles ?client variants on the fly.
- Svelte MorphIconProps now derives from svelte/elements (typos in SVG
  attrs fail the build, like lucide-svelte).
- Website: React/Vue/Svelte tabs in the landing code panel, roadmap and
  SEO updated across the site.
- CHANGELOG.md (Keep a Changelog): publish.yml now uses the version's
  entry as the GitHub Release notes, autogenerated notes as fallback.

feat: React Native binding over the reused dom driver (v1.4.0)

morphicons/react-native: the same MorphIcon as the web bindings — three
modes, shared lifecycle contract, lucide-style props, a11y defaults —
rendered through react-native-svg. The dom driver is the engine verbatim:
per-frame d writes go through Path.setNativeProps, outside the React
render. Reduced motion honors the OS setting via AccessibilityInfo
(best-effort query + reduceMotionChanged subscription).

- Mirrored mount suite + render/a11y suite + reduced-motion pins on
  happy-dom with react-native/react-native-svg mocked via mock.module
  (no react-test-renderer — deprecated in React 19): 156 tests total.
- Optional peers react-native >= 0.71 + react-native-svg >= 14; new
  ./react-native export, tsconfig, and 9 KB gzip gate (8.25 measured).
- Metro + package exports + ESM-only validated for real: Expo app in the
  external testbench bundles the local package headlessly (expo export).
- Website: React Native tab in the landing code panel, roadmap item
  moved to Shipped, JSON-LD softwareVersion 1.4.0.
- 1.3.0 was never published on its own; it ships as part of 1.4.0 (the
  changelog keeps both entries).

feat(website): expand the studio tray to 228 icons across the three libraries

Lucide grows to 115 live imports covering the most-used-icons canon (share,
phone, image, filter, help, cart, log-in/out...). Heroicons (55) and Tabler
(58) stop being hand-vendored: scripts/extract-vendor-icons.mjs extracts them
from the heroicons@2.2.0 and @tabler/icons@3.46.0 devDeps into
lib/vendor-icons.ts, keeping the 16 pre-existing icons byte-identical.
Labels are chosen for searchability (magnifying-glass -> search).

fix: quantize canonical d emission to 4 decimals (v1.4.1)

MorphIcon produced an SSR hydration mismatch on icons with arcs at
non-cardinal angles (lucide's eye): the canonical d was emitted at full
float precision, and arc→cubic conversion goes through trig whose last
ulp differs across JS engines, so the server's markup and the browser's
recomputation could disagree in the final digit. cubicsToPathD now
quantizes to 4 decimals (max deviation 5e-5 on the 24px grid,
invisible): one core change inherited by the four bindings' SSR/at-rest
markup, the driver's settle snap and fitIcon.

- Reproduced for real: canonicalD(Eye) differed byte-for-byte between
  Node (V8) and Bun (JSC) on 1.4.0; identical after the fix. Verified
  end-to-end in Next dev: the hydration overlay appears with 1.4.0 and
  is gone with the fixed build.
- Pinned by a 1-ulp perturbation test in core plus mirrored
  "engine-stable (quantized)" SSR tests in the four binding suites
  (161 tests); the round-trip bound moves from 1e-12 to the emission
  half-step 5e-5.
- README documents the why under "Serialization and canonical snap".

feat: morph icons rendered as CSS masks (SVG-markup input + createMorph auto-detect)

Reshaped per review — no per-library adapters, the capability lives under
the hood:

Input: IconInput now accepts an SVG markup string (leading '<' disambiguates
it from a d). It is generic-parsed to an IconNode, scanned for morphability
(fill-drawn/no-stroke, transforms and unsupported elements throw; <defs> and
other non-rendered containers are dropped) and auto-re-gridded onto 24 via its
viewBox. No branded /iconify subpath.

Output: createMorph picks its write strategy structurally from el.tagName — a
<path> (or a tagName-less fake / RN shim) gets the d attribute; any other
element is driven as a CSS mask-image. No branded /mask subpath; every binding
inherits it. Per-frame rasterization caveat documented.

Size gates renegotiated for the real capability (core parser ~0.6 KB, mask
writer ~0.55 KB); no version bump, no CLAUDE.md edits (release owner's call).

197 tests; typecheck/lint/size all green.

feat(adapters): opt-in format adapters entry: svgToIcon + double-buffered maskTarget

Reshape of the CSS-mask capability behind a single opt-in entry,
morphicons/adapters, so the unit of payment is the import: core, dom and
the four bindings stay byte-identical to main (the in-core shape charged
every consumer ~+0.6 KB gzip on core and ~+1.15 KB per binding).

- svgToIcon (input): SVG markup to IconInput. Keeps the v2 scan verbatim:
  fill-drawn rejection, non-rendered container stripping, viewBox auto-fit
  via fitIcon. Stray self-closed containers are skipped, not rejected.
- maskTarget (output): drives a CSS-mask element through a hidden PAIR of
  referenced <svg><mask><path> buffers; each d write lands on the back
  buffer and flips mask-image between url(#a) and url(#b). Two engine
  traps shaped this: a data-URI mask per frame never decodes in time in
  Chromium (blank flight), and WebKit does not repaint when a referenced
  mask's content mutates (frozen flight in Safari). Verified by eye in
  Chrome and Safari.
- Per-export size gates (size-limit named imports) pin each adapter as
  independently tree-shakeable: aggregate 4.03 KB, svgToIcon 3.34,
  maskTarget 0.70 gzip standalone.
- Decisions recorded in docs/adr/0001 (frozen core contracts, adapters
  entry) and docs/adr/0002 (mask mechanism, rejected alternatives), plus
  the CONTEXT.md glossary. 206 tests, strict typecheck x6, gates green.

feat(adapters): canvasTarget, 2D canvas out + release 1.6.0

Every d write becomes one stroke(new Path2D(d)): the icon stops being a
document node and becomes pixels you own (WebGL textures, chart sprites,
favicons, OffscreenCanvas in workers). Accepts an HTMLCanvasElement, an
OffscreenCanvas or a bare 2D context; min-side letterbox per write, so
devicePixelRatio stays the owner's business; color cascade (option >
lazily computed CSS color > owner's strokeStyle); clear:false for trails;
onWrite as the texture consumer's dirty signal. Hosts with their own
render loop composite a small dedicated canvas, never hand over their
context. 479 B gzip standalone, gated at 0.55 KB; suite grows to 225
tests including garbage-viewBox and 0x0-backing-store pins.

fix(react-native): keep the declarative d across Fabric commits + release 1.7.1 (#26)

On Fabric every commit rebuilds the native path from the props React declares, so the d the binding froze at mount overwrote the driver writes: a settled morph reset to the mount icon on any later render, and the same happened mid-flight, after a lazy imperative birth and mid-scrub in controlled mode.

React now declares the driver live d and a layout effect re-applies it when the driver moved between a render and its commit, with no state update per frame. The pre-paint effects are real layout effects on a device: the runtime probe is window, since React Native has no document.

The Path mock replays Fabric per-commit reconciliation and two new suites pin the behavior per state and per runtime.

Closes #25
